subject: math
title: Grade 8 Multiplying and Dividing Integers
seo_title: Grade 8 Multiplying and Dividing Integers Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Multiply and divide integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing integers for the Ontario curriculum: patterns that explain the sign rules, products of several integers, division checked by multiplication, order of operations, and word problems with falling temperatures and shared debts. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Same signs give a positive answer; different signs give a negative answer. (−3) × (−4) = 12 and (−12) ÷ 3 = −4.
key_sub: With three or more factors, count the negatives: an even count gives a positive product, an odd count a negative one. Check a division with multiplication: (−12) ÷ 3 = −4 because 3 × (−4) = −12.
body_html:
Multiplying is repeated addition

3 × (−4) means 3 groups of −4: (−4) + (−4) + (−4) = −12. On a number line, start at 0 and make 3 jumps of −4.

A pattern shows why (−) × (−) is positive

Each time the first factor goes down by 1, the product goes up by 4. Continue past 0 and the products become positive.

MultiplicationProduct
2 × (−4)−8
1 × (−4)−4
0 × (−4)0
(−1) × (−4)4
(−2) × (−4)8

The sign rules

Multiply or divide the numbers without their signs, then choose the sign. Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer. The same rules work for × and ÷.

SignsMultiplyDivide
positive and positive3 × 4 = 1212 ÷ 3 = 4
negative and negative(−3) × (−4) = 12(−12) ÷ (−3) = 4
positive and negative3 × (−4) = −1212 ÷ (−3) = −4
negative and positive(−3) × 4 = −12(−12) ÷ 3 = −4

With three or more factors, count the negative factors. An even count gives a positive product; an odd count gives a negative product.

Example 1

(−2) × 5 × (−3) × (−1)

2 × 5 × 3 × 1 = 30. There are 3 negative factors (odd), so the product is negative.

Answer: −30

Example 2

(−72) ÷ 8

72 ÷ 8 = 9. The signs are different, so the quotient is negative. Check: 8 × (−9) = −72.

Answer: −9

Order of operations

Brackets first, then exponents, then × and ÷ from left to right, then + and − from left to right. Write negative numbers in brackets so each sign is easy to see.

Example 3

(−4)² − 3 × (−2)

(−4)² = (−4) × (−4) = 16. Then 3 × (−2) = −6. Last, 16 − (−6) = 16 + 6 = 22.

Answer: 22

Example 4

In Barrie, the temperature is 4 °C at 7 p.m. and falls 3 °C each hour. What is it at 11 p.m.?

That is 4 hours. The change is 4 × (−3) = −12. Then 4 + (−12) = −8.

Answer: −8 °C

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
(−3) × (−4) = −12Same signs give a positive answer: 12
(−12) ÷ 3 = 4Different signs give a negative answer: −4
Adding instead of multiplying: 3 × (−4) = −13 × (−4) is 3 groups of −4: −12
(−3)² = −9(−3)² = (−3) × (−3) = 9
Working left to right: −8 + 3 × (−4) = 20Multiply before you add: −8 + (−12) = −20
Forgetting the starting temperatureAdd the change to the start: 4 + (−12) = −8

faq.q: How do you multiply and divide integers in Grade 8?
faq.a: Multiply or divide the numbers without their signs, then choose the sign: same signs give a positive answer and different signs give a negative answer. So (−3) × (−4) = 12 and (−12) ÷ 3 = −4.

faq.q: Why is a negative times a negative a positive?
faq.a: Look at the pattern 2 × (−4) = −8, 1 × (−4) = −4, 0 × (−4) = 0. Each step the product goes up by 4, so (−1) × (−4) = 4 and (−2) × (−4) = 8.

faq.q: Which Ontario Grade 8 expectation covers multiplying and dividing integers?
faq.a: Expectation B2.7 in the Number strand of the 2020 Ontario math curriculum: multiply and divide integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts.

faq.q: Do Grade 8 students in Ontario write EQAO?
faq.a: No. Ontario students write EQAO assessments in Grades 3 and 6, and the next math assessment is in Grade 9. Integer skills from Grade 8 are used all through Grade 9 math.

sets.title: Word problems: temperature, debts and more

items.q: After sunset, the temperature in Thunder Bay falls 2 °C each hour. What is the total change in temperature after 6 hours?
items.e: A fall of 2 °C each hour for 6 hours: 6 × (−2) = −12 °C.

items.q: After sunset, the temperature in Timmins falls 3 °C each hour. What is the total change in temperature after 5 hours?
items.e: A fall of 3 °C each hour for 5 hours: 5 × (−3) = −15 °C.

items.q: At 6 p.m., the temperature in Sudbury is 5 °C. It falls 2 °C each hour. What is the temperature at 11 p.m.?
items.e: From 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. is 5 hours. The change is 5 × (−2) = −10 °C. Then 5 + (−10) = −5 °C.

items.q: At 9 p.m., the temperature in Ottawa is −3 °C. It falls 3 °C each hour. What is the temperature at 1 a.m.?
items.e: From 9 p.m. to 1 a.m. is 4 hours. The change is 4 × (−3) = −12 °C. Then −3 + (−12) = −15 °C.

items.q: Five friends owe $750 together for a weekend cottage rental on Lake Muskoka, and they share the debt equally. Which integer shows each person’s share, in dollars?
items.e: A debt is negative: (−750) ÷ 5 = −150. Each person owes $150.

items.q: The six players on a basketball team owe $270 together for a bus to a tournament in Kingston, and they share the debt equally. Which integer shows each person’s share, in dollars?
items.e: A debt is negative: (−270) ÷ 6 = −45. Each person owes $45.

items.q: Four cousins owe $132 together for canoe rentals in Algonquin Park, and they share the debt equally. Which integer shows each person’s share, in dollars?
items.e: A debt is negative: (−132) ÷ 4 = −33. Each person owes $33.

items.q: Mateo is scuba diving near Tobermory in Georgian Bay. He starts at the surface (0 m) and goes down 3 m each minute for 7 minutes. Which integer shows his position?
items.e: Down is negative: 7 × (−3) = −21 m, so he is 21 m below the surface.

items.q: Lucas is scuba diving near Tobermory in Georgian Bay. He starts at the surface (0 m) and goes down 4 m each minute for 6 minutes. Which integer shows his position?
items.e: Down is negative: 6 × (−4) = −24 m, so he is 24 m below the surface.

items.q: Olivia pays $12 each month for a music app from her bank account. Which integer shows the change in her balance after 9 months, in dollars?
items.e: Paying out is negative: 9 × (−12) = −108.

items.q: Emma pays $25 each month for skating lessons from her bank account. Which integer shows the change in her balance after 6 months, in dollars?
items.e: Paying out is negative: 6 × (−25) = −150.

items.q: Overnight in North Bay, the temperature changed by −21 °C in 7 hours. It fell by the same amount each hour. What was the change each hour?
items.e: Divide the total change by the hours: (−21) ÷ 7 = −3 °C each hour.

items.q: During a dry August, the water level of a small lake near Kenora changed by −32 cm in 8 weeks. It fell by the same amount each week. What was the change each week?
items.e: Divide the total change by the weeks: (−32) ÷ 8 = −4 cm each week.

items.q: The water level in a reservoir falls 3 cm each day. After how many days will the change be −27 cm?
items.e: Each day the change is −3 cm. (−27) ÷ (−3) = 9 days (same signs, so positive).

items.q: At midnight in Kapuskasing, the temperature is 0 °C and falls 2 °C each hour. After how many hours will it be −16 °C?
items.e: Each hour the change is −2 °C. (−16) ÷ (−2) = 8 hours (same signs, so positive).
